prompt:
I need the front end for Stopwise. An audio library for independent walking-tour guides where they keep recordings of their own tours, alongside reference lectures they've bought, so they can listen back and tighten their narration.

Who's using it: Inês Carvalho, a self-employed licensed guide in Porto who has run her own food-and-history walks for six years. She records every new route on a lapel mic and listens back at home in the evenings. She's comfortable with the content but not technical.

What they're doing right now: She's listening to yesterday's trial run of a new Ribeira route at 1.25x speed, following along in the transcript. The walk ran 22 minutes over the planned two hours. She thinks most of that was at stop 4, the tile-covered church, where a guest's question pulled her into a long tangent. She wants to jump to where stop 4 starts, find where the tangent began and ended, and bookmark both points so she can cut that segment. Then she plans to play the 14-minute azulejo history lecture she bought last month, from the point where she left off, to check two dates she quoted on the walk.

What's in the system at this point: Her library has 37 of her own tour recordings, each 1h40m–2h30m long and split into chapters by stop. Yesterday's recording is 2h22m long with 9 stops; stop 4 runs from 0:48:10 to 1:21:55. Each recording has an auto-generated transcript with speaker labels (Inês / Guest), and she has added 6 bookmarks with short notes such as "cut here?" and "wrong year — 1739?". There are also 12 purchased reference lectures from a Portuguese heritage educator, each 9–40 minutes long; the azulejo lecture is 41% played, with her last position saved at 5:47. Her default playback speed is 1.25x, and she has a queue of 3 items waiting to play next.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
